Same lock is held while the operator sits at the production confirmation prompt, so an unattended 03:00 run fails if a manual prompt is left open (app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:45)

`return $this->fail(...)`: fail() never returns, so the `return` is redundant (app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:34)

v.rationale: All three meet the core spec and pass their suites. All three also passed a probe that makes a file genuinely undeletable on the real disk: the row is kept, the run continues and exits 1. impl-3 ranks first. It deletes in batches per chunk, which is the best fit for millions of rows. Its lock covers only the destructive section with a safe 6h TTL, and it has no real bugs; its tests are a bit thinner. impl-1 is the most framework-idiomatic, using Isolatable, partition and fail(), and has the richest tests. But its isolation lock is taken before handle(). A probe confirmed that a dry run fails while a purge is running, and a pending confirmation prompt blocks the scheduled run. It also adds an unrequested timezone and log file, and carries test ceremony including a misnamed test. impl-2 is the simplest and cleanest to read. It loses on per-row DELETE queries, a 1h lock TTL that a large first backlog could exceed, and a facade-replacing test double.
